answer: The tundra anchors each identity against a bonding curve: the n-th key registered pays n shale, credits a key earns only for its own attested work, one per epoch, non-transferable, from a fixed global per-epoch mint. A lotus, the attacker's clone, cannot buy or borrow shale, and k clones each earn slower from that fixed mint while the curve still charges the k-th k shale, so the per-head bill rises and the last clone waits on the order of k² epochs — a cost that cannot be split, since shale binds one key. Break: the tundra inflating the mint.
